result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A uses uniform 16px padding, an 8px heading gap that is clearly smaller than the 16px gutters, and one shared spacing scale, so it is consistent and modest. B is also good: its 12px heading gap is still under the 16px gutter, and centering the empty-state text helps the cell look balanced. But B's uneven 16px/20px padding and the extra min-height and :has() rules add complexity the 'keep it modest' request didn't need. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers use uniform 16px grid gaps and keep the heading-to-content gap smaller than the gap between panels (A uses 12px, B uses 8px). B is simpler and more consistent: its padding is the same on every side, and all spacing comes from one 8/16/24 scale. A's :has()-based centered empty state does help the cell look balanced, but it adds complexity, and its padding is uneven (16px top and bottom, 20px left and right).
